verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              भूय एव महाभाग्यं कथ्यतामित्यब्रवीत् पाण्डवः॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : The Pandavas again said, “Tell us again of the greatness (of the Kshatriyas).
verses.bhavadeepa: असाधावपि साधुत्वं प्रीत्या इष्टार्थदानं च महाभाग्यमित्यध्यायद्वयतात्पर्यम् ॥६॥

verses.sanskrit: अथाचष्ट मार्कण्डेयो महाराज वृषदर्भसेदुकनामानौ राजानौ नीतिमार्गरतावस्त्रोपास्त्रकृतिनौ॥२॥
verses.english: Markandeya said, "O great king, there were two kings, named Vrishadarbha and Seduka. Both of them were learned in the precepts of morality and skillful in the weapons of offence and defence.

verses.sanskrit: सेदुको वृषदर्भस्य बालस्यैव उपांशुव्रतमभ्यजानात् कुप्यमदेयं ब्राह्मणस्य॥३॥
verses.english: Seduka knew that Vrishadarbha had from his boyhood a mental vow, namely that he would never give no other metal to a Brahmana except gold and silver.

verses.sanskrit: अथ तं सेदुकं ब्राह्मणः कश्चिद्वेदाध्ययनसम्पन्न आशिषं दत्त्वा गुर्वर्थी भिक्षितवान्॥४॥
verses.english: Once upon a time, a Brahmana having completed his study of the Vedas, came to Seduka; and uttering a benediction upon him he begged (wealth for his preceptor);

verses.sanskrit: अश्वसहस्रं मे भवान् ददात्विति। तं सेदुको ब्राह्मणमब्रवीत्॥५॥
verses.english: Saying “Give me one thousand horses." Seduka spoke to the Brahmana,
"It is not possible for me to give you this for your preceptor.

verses.sanskrit: स त्वं गच्छ वृषदर्भसकाशम्। राजा परमधर्मज्ञो ब्राह्मण तं भिक्षस्व। स ते दास्यति तस्यैतदुपांशुव्रतमिति॥७॥
verses.english: Therefore go to Vrishadarbha; he is, O Brahmana, a (very) virtuous king; go and beg of him. He will give you, for it is his vow."

verses.sanskrit: अथ ब्राह्मणो वृषदर्भसकाशं गत्वा अश्वसहस्रमयाचत्। स राजा तं कशेनाताडयत्॥८॥
verses.english: Thereupon the Brahmana went TO Vrishadarbha and begged one thousand horses. That king (however) struck him with a whip. Then the Brahmana said, "I am innocent, why do you strike me thus?”

verses.sanskrit: एवमुक्त्वा तं शपन्तं राजाऽऽह। विप्र किं यो न ददाति तुभ्यमुताहोस्विद्ब्राह्मण्यमेतत्॥१०॥
verses.english: Having said this, he was going to curse the king, when the latter said,” Do you curse him who does not give you what you ask? Is this the conduct proper in a Brahmana?”

verses.sanskrit:
ब्राह्मण उवाच।
              राजाधिराज तव समीपं सेदुकेन प्रेषितो भिक्षितुमागतः। तेनानुशिष्टेन मया त्वं भिक्षतोऽसि॥११॥
verses.english: Brahmana said : O king of kings, sent to you by Seduka I came to you to beg. For your bad conduct, I am going to curse you.
verses.bhavadeepa: शपन्तं शापं दित्सन्तम् । हे विप्र यो न ददाति स्वीयं धनं तुभ्यं तस्मै वा एतत् शापदानमुचितम् । उताहोस्वित् एतद्ब्राह्मण्यं ब्राह्मणयोग्यं स्वीयमपि दित्सन् न शापयोग्यः । नापि शान्तिधर्मा ब्राह्मणः शापं दातुमर्हतीत्यर्थः ॥१०॥

verses.sanskrit:
राजोवाच।
              पूर्वाह्णे ते दास्यामि यो मेऽद्य बलिरागमिष्यति। यो हन्यते कशया कथं मोघं क्षेपणं तस्य स्यात्॥१२॥
verses.english: The king said : I shall now give by whatever tribute comes to me before the morning is expired. How can I send away a man empty-handed who has been whipped by me?

verses.sanskrit: इत्युक्त्वा ब्राह्मणाय दैवसिकामुत्पत्तिं प्रादात्। अधिकस्याश्वसहस्त्रस्य मूल्यमेवादादिति॥१३॥
verses.english: Markandeya said : Having said this, he gave the Brahmana whatever came to him that day which was not more than the value of one thousand horses.
verses.bhavadeepa: क्षेपणं दूरीकरणम् । अवश्यं स प्रसादनीय इत्यर्यः ॥१२॥
